text: NEAR Shoemaker became the first spacecraft to orbit an asteroid when it entered orbit around 433 Eros on February 14, 2000.
Though not designed as a lander, NEAR executed a gentle touchdown on the surface of Eros on February 12, 2001.
NEAR operated on the asteroid's surface, transmitting gamma-ray spectrometer data until February 28, 2001.
A final listening pass on December 10, 2002 attempted to contact the probe, but no signal was detected.
NASA concluded that the extreme cold of deep space on the asteroid surface (-150°C) eventually ended the spacecraft's operational life.
During its mission NEAR returned more than 160,000 images of asteroid Eros.
